html:
The Aaniiih, "White Clay people", are an Algonquian-speaking people of the northern Plains, in what are now northern Montana and southern Saskatchewan. French traders called them Gros Ventre, "big belly". Their language is closely related to that of the Arapaho, from whom they split long ago.

They became mounted bison hunters in the 1700s and traded at the Hudson's Bay Company posts on the Saskatchewan River. They were long allied with the Blackfoot Confederacy against the Cree and Assiniboine, but in the 1860s they broke with the Blackfoot. Smallpox and the end of the bison hit them hard. In 1888 they settled on the Fort Belknap Reservation in Montana, which they share with the Assiniboine. See Gros Ventre and the Blackfoot.
